title: Twelve 'sections pending verification' caveats closed against the enacted MS Act 2025 text
candidate_claim: GPT review pass 2A mapped the corpus's Merchant Shipping Act 2025 citations against the enacted text and authorised the closure of twelve caveats that read 'sections pending verification', 'cite at Part level' or 'exact 2025 section pending verification', each against a named section.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD ON EVERY MAPPING, AND THE CAVEAT ITSELF IS THE DEEPER FINDING. Each of the 23 authorised mappings was re-verified against the held text and confirmed. But a caveat is a DEBT, and this one had been rolled forward until QB9_H_CheatSheet was instructing candidates, as house doctrine, to 'cite the 2025 Act at Part level with sections pending verification'. An unverified claim that announces itself is safe; an unverified claim institutionalised as a style rule is not.

authority.extraction_hazards: TWO, recorded because one produced a false negative. (1) The Act's PDF separates a section number from its text with a 0x03 CONTROL BYTE as well as with a space, so a '^[0-9]+[.]\s' scan under-reports: s.319 was reported NOT FOUND on the first pass and is present exactly as authorised. A negative from a text scan is only evidence once the scan is proved able to find a positive. (2) The s.281(2) penalty table renumbers its rows 1..N, so a naive scan resolves 'section 15' to a table row about s.139; table rows must be excluded before a section number is resolved.
authority.part_structure: Verified from the Act: I ss.1-3; II ss.4-13; III ss.14-44; IV ss.45-53; V ss.54-113; VI ss.114-130; VII ss.131-143; VIII ss.144-152; IX ss.153-222; X ss.223-230; XI ss.231-232; XII ss.233-260; XIII ss.261-280; XIV ss.281-292; XV ss.293-324; XVI s.325.
authority.s_319_320_301: s.319(1): 'Without prejudice to any other power to make rules contained elsewhere in this Act, the Central Government may make rules generally to carry out the provisions of this Act.' s.320(1): all rules shall be published in the Official Gazette; s.320(3): every rule shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days, subject to modification or annulment. s.301: the Director-General may give BY NOTICE, CIRCULAR, ORDER OR GUIDELINES in writing such directions as he thinks fit to any vessel, seafarer, tindal, ship owner or agent, maritime training institute, recruitment placement service provider, port, or person or body of persons.
authority.s_324_the_narrow_limb: VERBATIM: 'The Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 (except Part XIV but not including section 411A therein) and the Coasting Vessels Act, 1838 is hereby repealed.' THIS IS NARROWER THAN 'EXCEPT PART XIV' - the saving is Part XIV MINUS s.411A, and s.411A is itself repealed. The authorisation said only 'the saved Part XIV limb as actually stated'; reading the provision is what produced the limb. Quoting s.411A is NOT a new 1958 assertion: it is quoted from inside s.324(1) of the 2025 Act. s.324(2) saves rules, offices, appointments, documents, fines, prosecutions and registrations made under the repealed enactments.
authority.s_83_62_12: s.83: a dispute under the seafarer's agreement is submitted to the shipping master, who must hear the parties and pass a reasoned written award within thirty days, extendable once by a further thirty for sufficient cause, conclusive as to the parties' rights, enforceable under the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 as if it were a decree of court, with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 expressly disapplied. s.62: seafarers may be engaged only by a licensed recruitment and placement service agency or by the owner of an Indian vessel; s.62(2) bars unlicensed business, engagement without a CDC and identity documents, and any fee charged to a seafarer. s.12(1): the Central Government may establish a shipping office and appoint thereto a shipping master and deputy/assistant shipping masters.
authority.part_xiv_penalties: s.281(1) residual penalty up to fifty thousand rupees where none is specially provided; s.281(2) the tabulated contravention and penalty schedule; s.282(1) the PRINCIPAL OFFICER is the authority for imposing the s.281(2) penalty, with appeal to the Director-General within thirty days under s.282(2); s.287(1) liability of the person in charge of and responsible to a company as well as the company; s.290(1) detention. Part XIV is ss.281-292, confirmed by Part XV beginning at s.293.
authority.registration: s.15(1): no vessel shall be an Indian vessel unless owned by (a) a citizen of India including an NRI or OCI, (b) a company or body established by or under a Central or State Act having its registered office or principal place of business in India, or (c) such other person or body as the Central Government may notify. THE ACT'S TERM OF ART IS 'INDIAN VESSEL', NOT 'INDIAN SHIP'. s.18: the principal officer of the Mercantile Marine Department, or such person as the Central Government authorises, shall be the Registrar of Indian vessels. s.20(9): 'Every Registrar shall keep a register book, make entries in that book and maintain the records of vessels registered under the provisions of this Act, in such manner as may be prescribed.'
authority.pollution: s.131 sets what Part VII applies to, including at (e) any incident of marine casualty or act relating to such casualty occurring with grave and imminent danger to the Indian coastline, coastal waters or related interests, including on the high seas. s.133(1): all vessels are under an obligation to prevent discharge or emission of harmful substances. s.138(1): the master shall report the particulars of an escape or likely escape; s.138(2): the Central Government may direct prevention of escape, removal of cargo or substances, movement of the vessel and removal of slicks. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE: 'contingency plan' 0 occurrences, 'OPRC' 0, 'NOS-DCP' 0, 'national oil spill' 0. The Act does NOT name or create the National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan.
authority.registry_locator_defect: SRC-MSACT-2025 carried the shipping-master definition at 's.93(c)'. THAT LOCATOR DOES NOT EXIST: s.93 is 'Inspection by shipping master, etc.', with clauses (a) and (b), sub-clauses (i)-(iv) and an Explanation defining 'international voyage'. The definition is the Explanation to s.91, clause (c) - 'For the purposes of this section ... (c) shipping master means a shipping master, (i) for the port at which the seafarer entered into, or is believed to have entered into, an agreement; or (ii) where the seafarer did not enter into an agreement in India, for the port to which the seafarer has returned, or is expected to return, on the completion of his latest voyage.' The PROPOSITION was correct; only the LOCATOR was wrong, which is why no candidate-facing gate could ever have caught it.

cards.supersession_note: E5 enriched this card and its pin is release evidence, unaltered here. E5 pins sha256(balanced_block_lf)[:16] = 1d4ea7d5216d503e; this record pins the same block in full, and the full digest BEGINS with E5's exact sixteen characters - the two conventions are one function at two truncations, verified rather than assumed. THIS IS THE FIRST CORRECTION IN THE CORPUS TO DESCEND FROM A TRUNCATED PIN, and recording it required a governance fix. oral_supersession._same_convention accepted only EQUAL widths, so every option was red: pinning at 64 gave DIGEST_CONVENTION_MISMATCH in the chain; pinning at 16 satisfied the chain but broke validate_corrections, which computes live and baseline digests in the 64-character convention; and omitting the claim left E5's own manifest_digests_match red on a legitimately corrected card. All three were tested, not assumed. The comparison is now prefix-tolerant across the two documented widths and compares on the common prefix, which a tampered card cannot satisfy.
